name: POST /api/leads/:id/assign - Assign or reassign a lead to a named owner
description: Moves a lead to an explicitly chosen owner, overriding whatever automatic routing decided, and records routing_method as 'manual' so an audit can distinguish a policy outcome from a person taking responsibility. A command against an existing lead, so it answers 200. Unlike POST /api/leads/:id/route this is deliberately NOT idempotent-by-skip: reassignment is the whole point, so an already-owned lead IS moved, and the response returns previous_owner_user_id so the caller can show what changed. THE RESPONSE CLOCK IS NOT RESTARTED - assigned_at and sla_due_at are preserved with COALESCE. The prospect has been waiting since the lead arrived, and resetting the deadline on each reassignment would let a lead be passed around indefinitely while always appearing to be within SLA. 'reason' is REQUIRED: an unexplained reassignment is not auditable. QA: depends on register (which creates the target owner), login and a captured lead.

transitions.notes: Sets owner_user_id to the named user and routing_method to 'manual'. Clears routing_rule_id, because a manual choice was not made by a rule. assigned_at and sla_due_at are PRESERVED - the original deadline stands.

testCases.name: Reassign the lead to a named owner
Reject a reassignment with no reason

errorCases.when: the id path parameter or owner_user_id is not a well-formed UUID, or reason is missing, blank or over 500 characters
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
no lead exists with the supplied id, or owner_user_id names no user
the target user exists but is deactivated, so cannot own a lead
